# Let me implement a cleaner algorithm to find diagonal pairs
# A diagonal pair = two cells with the SAME value where |dr|=1 AND |dc|=1

# For each demo, find which values have diagonal pairs
# And only those values extend

# Test input coordinates (from original analysis):
# (21,4)=4, (22,2)=9, (22,3)=4, (23,2)=1, (23,3)=9, (24,1)=1

test_input = [
    (21, 4, 4),
    (22, 2, 9),
    (22, 3, 4),
    (23, 2, 1),
    (23, 3, 9),
    (24, 1, 1),
]

print("Test input cells:")
for r, c, v in test_input:
    print(f"  ({r},{c}): {v}")

# For each cell, find if there's another cell with same value at diagonal distance
from collections import defaultdict

# Group by value
by_value = defaultdict(list)
for r, c, v in test_input:
    by_value[v].append((r, c))

# Check for diagonal pairs for each value
print("\nChecking for diagonal pairs (|dr|=1, |dc|=1):")
has_diag_pair = {v: False for v in by_value}
pairs = defaultdict(list)

for v in by_value:
    cells = by_value[v]
    for i, (r1, c1) in enumerate(cells):
        for j, (r2, c2) in enumerate(cells):
            if i == j:
                continue
            if abs(r2 - r1) == 1 and abs(c2 - c1) == 1:
                # Found a diagonal pair!
                has_diag_pair[v] = True
                if i < j:
                    pairs[v].append(((r1, c1), (r2, c2)))

for v in sorted(has_diag_pair.keys()):
    p = pairs[v]
    status = "HAS DIAGONAL PAIR" if has_diag_pair[v] else "NO diagonal pair"
    print(f"  Value {v}: {status}. Pairs: {p}")

print(f"\nValues with diagonal pairs: {[v for v in has_diag_pair if has_diag_pair[v]]}")
